summary: Verified surgical WebGL init fix in Game.js. Ran all 4 requested checks: (1) no-WebGL stub via page.add_init_script causes error-overlay to appear within 10s, loading-screen hides, no uncaught pageerrors; (2) happy-path boot without stub reaches main-menu, New Game starts, minimap shows with is-visible class, zero console errors; (3) error-overlay layout verified via screenshot (centered panel, dark backdrop, heading + Reload button); (4) window.__wnl API guards confirmed: _initFailed===true, start() no-op (does not throw), load() returns a resolved promise. Bug is fixed.

issues: Text contrast on the panel is very low — 'Something went wrong', the message, and the Reload label are barely legible against the dark green backdrop (see /app/test_reports/error_overlay.png). Consider brightening the panel text/border for the friendly-error use case, since the user sees only this.

action_items: Optional: improve contrast of the error-overlay panel text (see design_issues).

Optional: THREE.WebGLRenderer itself emits two console.error lines ('Error creating WebGL context.') before our try/catch runs — these appear as console errors in the no-WebGL run. They are third-party (three.js) internal logs, not uncaught exceptions, so acceptance for 'zero uncaught exceptions' is met (pageerror listener recorded 0). No action strictly required, but if silencing these is desired, wrap WebGLRenderer construction with a temporary console.error shim during the try{}.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and minimal: constructor sets this._initFailed, notifies via onError inside its own try/catch, returns before touching missing renderer. load() and start() are properly guarded. window.__wnl is still assigned in GameApp because the constructor returns `this` implicitly (JS default) — verified at runtime.

Nit: onLoaded is never called in the failed-init path, so `screen` state stays 'loading' — the overlay only hides because `showLoadingScreen` is gated on `!errorMsg`. This works but is subtle; consider explicitly setting screen to a terminal state on error for clarity (not required for the fix).
context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration only tested the WebGL init failure fix. Prior iteration_2 was Phase 5 sign-off; Phase 6 broader regression is still pending a separate testing pass per E1's note. Preview URL: https://wilderness-wgl.preview.emergentagent.com. To reproduce the no-WebGL path, install a page.add_init_script that returns null for /webgl/i getContext requests before navigation.
rca of the issue: Original bug: in the constructor's WebGLRenderer try/catch, after calling onError(e) the code did `throw e;`. Because `new Game(...)` was called synchronously from GameApp's useEffect (not wrapped in try/catch), the throw unwound out of the constructor, `gameRef.current = game` was never assigned, and setErrorMsg had run — but subsequent `game.load().then(...)` on an undefined game would blow up as another uncaught error, or (if the throw preceded the setErrorMsg microtask) the loading screen would stay because the initial render still saw `screen==='loading'` and no errorMsg. Fix removes the throw and installs _initFailed guards on load()/start(). Verified: no uncaught pageerror, error-overlay renders, guards no-op cleanly.
